A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rCM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GenEval and VBench evaluations, generated image/video samples, a regularization-weight ablation, and numerical JVP-error measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative sCM video outputs in Appendix E, Figure 9.

M1.justification: The rCM objective, score regularizer, rollout procedure, time-derivative stabilization, and JVP infrastructure are unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 and the implementation listing are retained.

E1.justification: Training data sources and T2I, T2V, and I2V coverage remain unchanged, as do GenEval and VBench coverage. The additional Wan video examples remain within the existing T2V task rather than establishing a distinct evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained quantitative and qualitative comparisons is unchanged. New Figure 9 displays only sCM outputs; its references to discrete-time CMs and DMD do not constitute an added evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New Figure 9 extends the reported four-step sCM video evaluation to Wan2.1-14B alongside 1.3B, with panels labeled 5k and 20k training iterations, respectively. This adds an evaluation configuration without revising the existing benchmark protocols or establishing that earlier runs changed.

E4.justification: Figure 9 extends the qualitative case study of sCM scalability and remaining visual-quality limitations with video examples at two model sizes. The regularization-weight ablation, sCM-versus-sCTM comparison, and BF16 JVP-error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report four repetitions of the 553 GenEval prompts and five random seeds for Figure 7's diversity illustrations. No repeated-run, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: v3 adds qualitative four-step sCM video results in Figure 9. Tables 1–3, Figure 7's VBench scores, and the retained JVP-error plots are unchanged; the addition does not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, derivative expressions, attention-JVP derivation, and sCTM equations are unchanged. The new introductory schematic illustrates the existing forward/reverse-divergence framing without introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable JVP infrastructure, score-regularized consistency distillation, and few-step quality/diversity benefits. The principal novelty and acceleration claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly qualifies its discussion of JVP applications by excluding discrete variants such as masked diffusion. The interpretations of error accumulation, quality/diversity trade-offs, and few-step limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly defines T as the number of latent video frames, clarifying the video time-sampling formula. Figure 9 also supplies checkpoint iteration counts; existing implementation details, hyperparameters, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to DiffusionNFT, Diffusion Bridge Implicit Models, and three masked-diffusion works, and expands the connection to diffusion reinforcement learning. The main research positioning remains intact; publication updates for retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Limited introductory and related-work edits add offline/on-policy terminology and explanatory context. Affiliations and acknowledgments change, and a new More Results appendix shifts the former discussion and prompt appendices from E/F to F/G.

P2.justification: v3 adds an unnumbered introductory schematic and the Figure 9 video montage. Figure 5 and Table 3 move to later pages, while the previous Figures 9–10 become Figures 10–11; existing displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added video examples, including Wan2.1-14B sCM outputs, provide modest additional evidence for the scalability and quality-limitations discussion. Defining latent-frame T in Table 4 also improves reproducibility. These gains are limited: the new montage provides no matched discrete-CM/DMD comparison, and the main quantitative evidence and statistical support remain unchanged.
